html:
The Semiahmoo are a Coast Salish people of Semiahmoo Bay and Boundary Bay, on the coast where British Columbia meets Washington state today. They spoke a dialect of Northern Straits Salish.

They fished for salmon with reef nets, dug clams and gathered berries and roots, travelling the bays by canoe. Their neighbours included the Tsawwassen to the north and the Nooksack inland.

The Oregon Treaty of 1846 drew the border between British and American land along the 49th parallel, right through their home. The Semiahmoo First Nation today has a small reserve beside White Rock, British Columbia.
